    AI Overview
    Péter Magyar, who defeated Viktor Orbán in the 2026 Hungarian election, is a center-right politician leading the Tisza Party (Respect and Freedom). His platform centers on anti-corruption, rebuilding democratic institutions, improving relations with the European Union, and restoring the rule of law while bridging Hungary's left-right divide. 
    Key Political Views 
    • Anti-Corruption & Democracy: Magyar rose to prominence by exposing corruption within the Orbán government and promising to hold officials accountable. He vows to restore checks and balances, strengthen the judiciary, and bring in an era of transparency.
    • EU Relations: He advocates for repairing Hungary's relationship with the European Union to unlock frozen development funds, positioning himself as pro-European compared to his predecessor.
    • Economic Policy: Magyar focuses on improving living standards, boosting Hungary's struggling economy, and addressing the nation's healthcare system.
    • Foreign Policy & Energy: While aiming to end Hungary's heavy dependence on Russian energy by 2035, he has described his approach toward Moscow as needing "pragmatic relations," rather than total alienation.
    • Political Identity: Often described as a "conservative liberal" or a "pragmatic centrist," he aims to move beyond the traditional, deeply polarized left-right, ideological divide in Hungarian politics.
    • Social Issues: During his campaign, he largely focused on domestic and economic issues rather than divisive social topics, showing a more moderate stance. 
    Background
    A former member of the Fidesz party ecosystem, Magyar was once considered a regime insider before becoming its most significant challenger, channeling public anger into a political reform movement.
